text: I learned stonework from my father.
He taught me that stone remembers pressure.
The monument is older than the village, but not uniform in construction.
Different sections show different tool marks.
Some parts were clearly added later.
Others appear to have been repaired repeatedly over unknown time spans.
Ren believes these differences represent symbolic phases.
I believe they represent functional repairs.
Both interpretations might be partially correct.
The central plaza has shifted slightly over many years.
Most people do not notice this.
The shift is not dangerous yet.
But it is measurable.
Certain stones in the monument have been replaced multiple times.
The replacements do not match original material sources.
That suggests trade or relocation of stone over long distances.
The small ancient building near the temple uses different joining techniques than newer structures.
It may predate current construction knowledge.
I have documented tool mark inconsistencies across the monument base.
No official record explains these differences.
Toma maintains ritual integrity but does not question structural origin.
That is not his role.
Ikan once asked about hidden chambers beneath the monument.
I told him there are stress points consistent with hollow spaces below.
I did not elaborate.
After the Night of Ash, some stone sections shifted slightly.
The shift was minor but noticeable in alignment measurements.
Repairs after that event do not fully match previous structural patterns.
Someone altered construction details during repairs.
I do not know who.
